narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history had the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. You have no previous credits or all paid credits, a rare profile that appears in only 1% of approved applicants and signals higher uncertainty to the model. 

The status of your checking account was the second most important factor and worked in your favor. Having ≥200 DM or salary assignments is relatively uncommon (only 9.7% of applicants) and the model viewed this positively, pulling the prediction toward approval. 

The requested loan duration of 9 months was the third key driver and also helped your case. This is substantially shorter than the 19-month average among approved loans, which the model interpreted as lower risk.

Although two of the top three factors spoke in your favor, the negative impact of your credit history was strong enough to outweigh them and tip the decision toward denial.

You should focus on building a more established credit history by taking out and successfully repaying smaller loans or credit cards over time. Once you have a positive track record of existing paid credits, reapply. This single change is likely to significantly improve your chances of approval. (248 words)
